summary: A linked list stores values in separate nodes, each pointing to the next one. Adding at the front is O(1), but reaching index i takes i steps.
notes: for (Node current = head; current != null; current = current.next) is the standard traversal loop.
insertAt sets newNode.next before current.next. Reversing those two lines loses the rest of the list.
The Node class is typed: its value is a String and next can only point to another Node or null.
pitfall: Calling insertAt with an index past the end makes current become null, and current.next throws NullPointerException.
